arxiv-2107-03499.title: Non co-preservation of the 1 / 2 1/2 & 1 / ( 2 ​ l + 1 ) 1/(2l+1) –rational caustics along deformations of circles
arxiv-2107-03499.creator: V. Kaloshin, C. E. Koudjinan
arxiv-2107-03499.description: Abstract For any given positive integer l l , we prove that every plane deformation of a circle which preserves the 1 / 2 1/2 and 1 / ( 2 ​ l + 1 ) 1/(2l+1) –rational caustics is trivial i.e. the deformation consists only of similarities (rescalings plus isometries).

arxiv-2404-05536.title: On Optimal MMSE Channel Estimation for One-Bit Quantized MIMO Systems Thanks: M. Ding, I. Atzeni, and A. Tölli are with the Centre for Wireless Communications, University of Oulu, Finland (e-mail: {minhua.ding, italo.atzeni, antti.tolli}@oulu.fi). A. L. Swindlehurst is with the Center for Pervasive
arxiv-2404-05536.creator: Minhua Ding, Italo Atzeni
arxiv-2404-05536.description: Abstract This paper focuses on the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) channel estimator for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems with one-bit quantization at the receiver side. Despite its optimality and significance in estimation theory, the MMSE estimator has not been fully investigated in this context due to its general nonlinearity and computational complexity.

arxiv-2502-07973.title: Cost Effectiveness Analyses for Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trials
arxiv-2502-07973.creator: Lina M. Montoya, Elvin Geng, Harriet F. Adhiambo, Eliud Akama, Starley B. Shade, Assurah Elly, Thomas Odeny, Maya Petersen
arxiv-2502-07973.description: Abstract Sequential multiple assignment randomized trials (SMARTs) have grown in popularity in recent years, and many of their study protocols propose conducting a cost effectiveness analysis of the adaptive strategies embedded within them. The cost effectiveness of these regimes is often proposed to be assessed using incremental cost effectiveness ratios (ICERs).

arxiv-2511-04806.title: From Brunn-Minkowski to Prékopa-Leindler and Borell-Brascamp-Lieb: discrete inequalities.
arxiv-2511-04806.creator: Peter van Hintum
arxiv-2511-04806.description: Abstract We consider a general way to obtain Prékopa-Leindler and Borell-Brascamp-Lieb type inequalities from Brunn-Minkowski type inequalities and provide numerous examples. We use the same heuristic to prove a discrete version of the Prékopa-Leindler and Borell-Brascamp-Lieb inequalities for functions over ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} .

arxiv-2602-09033.title: Schrödinger Was Right! He left his “wavefunction” program incomplete, but nonlinear math and chaos theory can finish the job
arxiv-2602-09033.creator: W. David Wick
arxiv-2602-09033.description: Abstract 1 1 1 email: wdavid.wick@gmail.com 1 Introduction Now that we have reached the centennial of Erwin Schrödinger’s seminal paper introducing the wavefunction theory of matter, it is right and proper to inquire as to its legacy. It is undeniable that today every paper in atomic physics cites his 1926 equation in the first paragraph.

pmc-10733756.description: treaty of the World Trade Organization.1 Patent enforcement involves preventing generic manufacturers from offering patented medicines at competitive prices. So protected from competition, patented medicines are often sold with exorbitant monopoly markups that effectively deprive many poor patients of access to them.

pmc-11452937.title: La (NO3)3 substantially fortified Glycyrrhiza uralensis’s resilience against salt stress by interconnected pathways
pmc-11452937.creator: Tingting Jia, Junjun Gu, Miao Ma
pmc-11452937.description: The taproot of Glycyrrhiza uralensis is globally appreciated for its medicinal and commercial value and is one of the most popular medicinal plants. With the decline of wild G. uralensis resources, cultivated G. uralensis has become a key method to ensure supply. However, soil salinization poses challenges to G. uralensis cultivation and affects the yield and quality of it.

pmc-11453981.creator: Theophilus Tettey, Sohyoung Kim, Kaustubh Wagh, Qizong Lao, Louis R Schiltz, Agustina Lafuente, Diana A Stavreva, Diego Martin Presman, Deborah P Merke, Gordon L Hager

Hager: None.The glucocorticoid receptor (GR) is a hormone regulated transcription factor which binds chromatin to regulate many genes, including stress-response and inflammatory genes.

pmc-12380877.title: Hearing loss: a global view for gene therapy approaches and challenges
pmc-12380877.creator: Nagham Maher Elbagoury
pmc-12380877.description: Hearing loss (HL) is a global issue that affects the quality of life. The incidence of the prelingual form reaches 1: 500 live births, where inherited HL represents the most frequent form. The early diagnosis and intervention to restore hearing might help in reaching near-normal speech milestones in congenital HL cases.

pmc-12397600.title: Maternal physical and social characteristics that influence the occurrence of preeclampsia/eclampsia and hemorrhage in Eastern Region of Ghana. A prospective cohort study
pmc-12397600.creator: James Atampiiga Avoka, Elvis Junior Dun-Dery, Augustine Ankomah, Agartha Ohemeng, Issah Seidu, Frederick Dun-Dery
pmc-12397600.description: Background:Preeclampsia/eclampsia places grave barriers to the successful reduction of maternal mortality and morbidity. These barriers have significant adverse outcomes for most women especially in sub-Saharan Africa, with Ghana contributing 88.7% of preeclampsia cases in Africa.Aim:The aim of this study is to evaluate the maternal, physical and social characteristics that influence the occurrence of preeclampsia/eclampsia in Eastern Region of Ghana.

pmc-12427273.title: Genetic Diversity and Population Structure of Five Pig Breeds from Chongqing, China
pmc-12427273.creator: Xi Long, Lidan Zhang, Yu Pan, Liang Zhang, Zhi Tu, Lijuan Zhang, Qing Wang, Hongmei Pan, Zongyi Guo
pmc-12427273.description: Simple SummaryChongqing, a municipality directly under the Central Government of China, is located in the southwest of the country and has a subtropical monsoon climate. Five pig breeds with distinct genetic characteristics evolved in this region due to climate, topography, and human activities. These breeds have high-quality meat and are resistant to heat, humidity, and disease.

pmc-12434923.title: Preparation of spirocyclic oxindoles by cyclisation of an oxime to a nitrone and dipolar cycloaddition
pmc-12434923.creator: Beth L Ritchie, Alexandra Longcake, Iain Coldham
pmc-12434923.description: Oxindoles are an important class of compounds with significant biological activities. Spirocyclic derivatives are present in a variety of natural products. We describe here the formation of spirooxindoles using an intermolecular nitrone cycloaddition reaction. The nitrone dipole was prepared in situ by cyclisation of an oxime, itself prepared in situ from an aldehyde.

pmc-12831313.title: Loss of measles, mumps, and rubella immunity in pediatric cancer survivors following chemotherapy
pmc-12831313.creator: Kanokkan Nakasuwan, Sujittra Chaisavaneeyakorn, Samart Pakakasama, Chonnamet Techasaensiri, Nopporn Apiwattanakul, Sophida Boonsathorn
pmc-12831313.description: ObjectivesPediatric cancer survivors are at increased risk for vaccine-preventable diseases due to treatment-related immunosuppression. This study aimed to assess serological status for measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) following chemotherapy and identify factors associated with antibody loss.ResultsFifty-four pediatric cancer survivors (mean age 12.5 years) were evaluated at a median of 2.5 years (IQR 1.2, 5.4) after completing chemotherapy.

pmc-13363664.title: The Role of Self-Compassion and Body Perception in Predicting Psychological Safety
pmc-13363664.creator: Andrea Poli, Mario Miccoli
pmc-13363664.description: Background/Objectives: Psychological safety is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant construct linked to emotional regulation, interpersonal functioning, and trauma-related processes. Emerging evidence suggests that psychological safety may depend not only on embodied experiences of bodily regulation but also on how individuals relate to themselves under conditions of distress.

pmc-13601951.title: Acute caffeine strategies for improving performance in combat sports: a structured narrative review
pmc-13601951.creator: Jingang Fan, Yike Li, Dongchen Li, Hansen Li, Guodong Zhang
pmc-13601951.description: ObjectiveThis structured narrative review updates and contextualizes evidence on acute caffeine strategies in combat sports, with emphasis on performance effects, delivery form, combined interventions, and factors that may explain inconsistent findings.MethodsA structured literature search was conducted in Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, PubMed, and SPORTDiscus.
